clasificacion.titulo_pagina: Binary trend classification · Ernesto Investing AI
clasificacion.sub: Will each asset go up or down? There are only two classes: UP or DOWN.
clasificacion.ficha_que_hace: Uses {n} models ({ml} Machine Learning and {dl} Deep Learning) to estimate whether each asset's price {h} sessions from now will be higher than today's. There are only two answers: UP or DOWN.
clasificacion.ficha_que_tan_bien: Accuracy from {exmin} to {exmax} and AUC from {aucmin} to {aucmax} on {prueba}. {comparacion}
clasificacion.ficha_por_que: Each cell is the probability of UP that one model gives for one asset. The consensus is the average of the {n} models, and confidence tells how far that average is from {mitad}.
clasificacion.ficha_controlas: The asset group, the model family, which models are shown and whether you see only your watchlist.
clasificacion.ficha_ignorar: You can hide any model you do not trust. None of this is an order to buy or sell.
clasificacion.sin_modelos: No model is visible. Tick one under “Visible models” or change the family.
clasificacion.sin_filas: No asset matches the filters. Change the group or untick “My watchlist only”.
clasificacion.mapa_titulo: Heatmap: probability of UP by asset and model
clasificacion.mapa_ayuda: Each cell says UP or DOWN with its symbol and the probability of UP. Pick an asset to see its consensus.
clasificacion.mapa_caption: Probability of UP from each model for each asset; every cell says UP or DOWN with a symbol.
clasificacion.votos_aria: Votes: {sube} for UP and {baja} for DOWN
clasificacion.consenso_explica: Votes from the {n} models: {sube} for UP and {baja} for DOWN. The mean probability of going up is {prob}. The consensus is {senal}, with {confianza} confidence.
clasificacion.confianza_explica: Confidence measures how far the mean probability is from {mitad}: it is high from {alta} points away and medium from {media}.
clasificacion.consenso_recuerda: Remember: on the test these models were right between {min} and {max} of the time. It is a weak hint, not a certainty.
clasificacion.metricas_ayuda: Pick a model to see its confusion matrix. The column headers sort the table.
clasificacion.mc_caption: Confusion matrix for {modelo}: what the model said versus what happened
clasificacion.mc_frase: Of the {dijo} days it said UP, it was right {vp} times; of the {dijo_baja} days it said DOWN, it was right {vn} times. The test covers {n} days.
clasificacion.honestidad_p1: If you flip a coin {cien} times to guess whether a price goes up or down, you are right about {mitad} times. These {n} models were right between {min} and {max} out of every {cien} on the test: only slightly better than the coin. They are a weak hint, not a certainty.
clasificacion.honestidad_p2: Also, a model that always said UP would have been right {base} of the time, because on {prueba} the price rose that share of the time. That is why next to each signal you see the consensus, the confidence and the metrics.
clasificacion.escuchando_mapa: Playing the consensus of {n} assets, top to bottom: a rising tone is ▲ UP ({sube}) and a falling one is ▼ DOWN ({baja}).
clasificacion.prueba_sesiones: a test of {sesiones} sessions ({n} observations: each asset in each session)
clasificacion.comp_ninguno: None of the {m} models beats the “always UP” rule, which is right {base} of the time.

comp_ninguno_mitad.one: None of the {m} models beats the “always UP” rule, which is right {base} of the time, and {n} is right less than half of the time.
comp_ninguno_mitad.other: None of the {m} models beats the “always UP” rule, which is right {base} of the time, and {n} are right less than half of the time.

comp_algunos.one: {n} of {m} models beats the “always UP” rule, which is right {base} of the time; the best reaches {exmax}.
comp_algunos.other: {n} of {m} models beat the “always UP” rule, which is right {base} of the time; the best reaches {exmax}.

regresion.sub: Where could the price go? Each model projects a path; the band shows how much they disagree.
regresion.ficha_que_hace: Projects each asset's price for the next {h} sessions with {n} models ({ml} Machine Learning and {dl} Deep Learning) and summarizes their paths with the median and a band.
regresion.ficha_que_tan_bien: On the test, the mean price error (MAPE) ranges from {mapemin} to {mapemax}. {mejora} The R² of returns ranges from {r2min} to {r2max}: they explain very little of what happens.
regresion.ficha_por_que: The thick line is the median of the {n} models; the band runs from the most pessimistic to the most optimistic model without the extremes (p10–p90), and the cone shows where {nivel} of the scenarios would fall given the asset's volatility.
regresion.ficha_controlas: The asset, the model family, which models are drawn, how much history you see and whether the band and the cone are shown.
regresion.ficha_ignorar: Hide any model you do not trust or look only at the band. A forecast is not an order to buy or sell.
regresion.tabla_titulo: {ticker}: the {n} prices projected by the median, with the p10–p90 band and the cone
regresion.resumen: {ticker}: the median of {n} models projects {precio} on {fecha}. The central models (p10–p90) lie between {p10} and {p90}, and given volatility {nivel} of the scenarios fall between {inf} and {sup}.
regresion.sin_banda: A line without a band would convey a certainty that does not exist: that is why the band and the cone are on.
regresion.verif_titulo: Brief check: last price of the median
regresion.verif_caption: Checks of the projected return of {ticker}
regresion.verif_literal: Brief: the final median matches “last × (1 + return)” within {tol}
regresion.verif_inversa: Data contract: the median's return, rounded to {d} decimals, is the published one
regresion.verif_global: Across the {total} assets, the brief's check passes in {literal} and the contract's in {inversa}. The brief's check fails in: {lista}.
regresion.verif_explica: The difference comes from the published return being rounded to {d} decimals: on a high price, that rounding exceeds one cent. The data is not corrected; both checks are shown.
regresion.metricas_ayuda: Pick a model to highlight its line in the chart. The column headers sort the table.
regresion.metricas_caption: Metrics of each regressor on the out-of-sample test
regresion.def_mape: Mean percentage error of the price at the end of the horizon. Lower is better.
regresion.def_mae: Mean error of the horizon return, in percentage points.
regresion.def_rmse: Like MAE, but penalizes large errors more.
regresion.def_r2: How much of the variation in returns the model explains: zero is nothing and one is everything.
regresion.def_mejora: How much it lowers MAPE compared with assuming the price does not change. Positive: the model adds something.
regresion.mejora_todos: All {n} models beat “the price does not change”, but only by {mejmin} to {mejmax}.
regresion.mejora_algunos: {mejoran} of {n} models beat “the price does not change”, but only by {mejmin} to {mejmax}; the other {resto} do worse (down to {peor}).
regresion.mejora_ninguno: None of the {n} models beats “the price does not change”: they range from {peor} to {mejor}.

optimizador.titulo_pagina: Optimizer: Markowitz, NSGA-II and NSGA-III · Ernesto Investing AI
optimizador.sub: Each point is a possible portfolio: further right, more risk; higher up, more expected return.
optimizador.ficha_que_hace: Shows portfolios that split the money among the {n} eligible assets, with at most {tope} per asset: the Markowitz curve and the NSGA-II and NSGA-III fronts.
optimizador.ficha_que_tan_bien_profesor: In Course mode, the Markowitz curve is computed on the course's synthetic data (we reproduce it with the same figures); the NSGA-II and NSGA-III fronts are simulated: no evolutionary algorithm was run. Even so they follow the theory: at equal return, NSGA-II is on average {media} volatility points above Markowitz. Expected return is an estimate, not a promise.
optimizador.ficha_que_tan_bien_real: The fronts were computed with the real data. At the same return, NSGA-II sits on average {media} volatility points above Markowitz. Expected return is an estimate, not a promise.
optimizador.ficha_por_que: Only assets with an UP consensus from the classifiers and a positive projection from the regressors are included. Pick a point to see which assets it holds and with what weight.
optimizador.ficha_controlas: Which curves and fronts you see, whether the Markowitz curve uses the whole universe or only the eligible assets, and which portfolio you inspect.
optimizador.ficha_ignorar: You do not have to use any of these portfolios. They are examples of the risk–return trade-off, not investment advice.
optimizador.ayuda_teclado: With the focus on the chart: left and right arrows move through the points of a series, up and down change series, Enter shows its composition.
optimizador.recalculo_profesor: In Course mode the fronts are read from the course file and are not recomputed. Recomputing in your browser is available in Real mode.
optimizador.grafico_titulo: Risk versus return of the portfolios
optimizador.tabla_titulo: All visible points, with their return, volatility, Sharpe and CVaR
optimizador.resumen: Selected portfolio: {sel}. The chart shows the Markowitz curve ({nm} points), the NSGA-II front ({n2} portfolios) and the NSGA-III front ({n3} portfolios).
optimizador.sin_series: No series is visible. Turn one on under “What is shown”.
optimizador.cvar_explica: CVaR: on the worst day out of every twenty, this portfolio would lose {cvar} on average.
optimizador.explica_markowitz: For each target return it finds the portfolio with the lowest volatility. It is a mathematical problem with an exact solution: that is why it is a curve and marks the limit of what is possible.
optimizador.explica_nsga2: An evolutionary algorithm with two objectives at once (more return and less volatility). It tries many portfolios, crosses and mutates the best ones over several generations and keeps those that nobody beats on both objectives.
optimizador.explica_nsga3: Like NSGA-II, but with a third objective, CVaR (the loss on the worst days), and reference directions to spread the solutions. Its color shows the CVaR.
optimizador.debajo_titulo: Why do the NSGA fronts sit slightly below Markowitz?
optimizador.debajo_texto: Evolutionary algorithms are approximate searches with a limited number of generations: they get close to the exact limit without reaching it. NSGA-III also spreads its portfolios to look after a third objective, CVaR, and gives up some risk–return efficiency. In this data, at the same return, NSGA-II has on average {m2} more volatility points (at most {x2}) and NSGA-III {m3} (at most {x3}).
optimizador.debajo_profesor: In Course mode these fronts were built from the Markowitz curve with small perturbations: they show the expected shape, but no evolutionary algorithm was run.
optimizador.debajo_real: In Real mode these fronts were computed with a real evolutionary algorithm on the Yahoo Finance data.
optimizador.verif_global: Brief check: of the {puntos} points on the fronts, {cumplen} have weights summing to one within {tol} and no weight above the {tope} cap.
optimizador.criterio: Criterion: the classifiers' consensus is UP and the regressors' median projection is positive.
optimizador.pedido_ok: {ticker} is eligible: {votos} of {n} classifiers say UP and its projection is {retorno}.
optimizador.pedido_consenso: {ticker} is not eligible because the classifiers' consensus is {consenso} (even though its projection is {retorno}).
optimizador.pedido_retorno: {ticker} is not eligible because its projection is {retorno} (even though the consensus is {consenso}).
optimizador.pedido_ambos: {ticker} is not eligible: the consensus is {consenso} and its projection is {retorno}.
optimizador.recalculo_real: You can recompute the frontiers in your browser with the real closes and another estimation window. The expected return will be the historical mean of that window (not the regressors' projection), so the result does not match the file.
optimizador.debajo_navegador: These fronts were recomputed in your browser with a real evolutionary algorithm on Yahoo Finance closes.
optimizador.ayuda_zoom: To separate points that overlap, zoom in with two fingers on the chart (or Ctrl and the mouse wheel); you can also pick them from the table.

portafolios.titulo_pagina: Portfolios at three risk levels · Ernesto Investing AI
portafolios.sub: Three portfolios from the NSGA-II front for different risk appetites. Compare them, pick one and, if you want, take it to Paper trading.
portafolios.ficha_que_hace: Suggests {n} portfolios taken from the NSGA-II front, each with a different balance between expected return and risk.
portafolios.ficha_que_tan_bien: The figures are estimates: expected return comes from projections with little predictive power. In Backtesting you can see how each profile would have done in the past. See them as examples, not promises.
portafolios.ficha_por_que: Each asset comes with its reason: how many classifiers say UP and how much the regressors' median projects.
portafolios.ficha_controlas: Which level you pick, which assets you exclude (the weights are spread again) and how much money you take to trading.
portafolios.ficha_ignorar: You can exclude assets or use none of the portfolios. None of this is investment advice.
portafolios.cvar_llano: On the worst {cola} of days you would lose {cvar} on average.

backtesting.sub: How would the three profiles have done in the past, compared with the market? Shown exactly as it came out.
backtesting.ficha_que_hace: Simulates what would have happened to {n} portfolio profiles over {sesiones} sessions, from {inicio} to {fin}, rebalancing every month using only the information available on each date.
backtesting.ficha_que_tan_bien: In this period, {superan} of {n} profiles beat {ref}. A backtest does not predict the future: it shows how a rule would have behaved in one specific past.
backtesting.ficha_por_que: Every month the rule filters the assets that had been rising, estimates risk from the last months and splits the money according to the profile. Below, the figures explain why each portfolio won or lost against the market.
backtesting.ficha_controlas: Which series you see in the charts (checkboxes or legend), which portfolio and date you inspect in the timeline and, in Real mode, on which date the period ends.
backtesting.ficha_ignorar: A good or bad past result commits you to nothing. This is not investment advice.
backtesting.metricas_ayuda: The column headers sort the table. The portfolio rows are marked.
backtesting.metricas_caption: Metrics of the three portfolios and the market references
backtesting.curvas_tabla: Capital of each series in each session
backtesting.curvas_resumen: All series start at {base}. Final value: {lista}.
backtesting.dd_tabla: Fall from the previous peak of each series in each session
backtesting.verif: Brief check: in {ok} of {n} series the curve's final value matches the total return within {tol} points (largest difference {max}).
backtesting.nota_tope: Note on the course data: {lista} per asset, although the declared cap is {tope}. It is an inconsistency in the material; it is shown as it comes.
backtesting.tl_inicial: This is the first rebalance: the portfolio starts from cash.
backtesting.tl_turnover: It bought and sold {turnover} of the portfolio value compared with the previous rebalance (without the price changes between dates; the portfolio average in the file is {medio}).
backtesting.frase_supera: It ended at {retorno}, versus {refRet} for {ref}: {dif} points more.
backtesting.frase_no_supera: It ended at {retorno}, versus {refRet} for {ref}: {dif} points less.
backtesting.frase_sharpe_mejor: Its Sharpe ({sharpe}) was better than {ref}'s ({refSharpe}): it earned more per unit of risk.
backtesting.frase_sharpe_peor: Its Sharpe ({sharpe}) was worse than {ref}'s ({refSharpe}): it earned less per unit of risk.
backtesting.frase_mdd_peor: Its worst fall ({mdd}) was deeper than {ref}'s ({refMdd}).
backtesting.frase_mdd_mejor: Its worst fall ({mdd}) was shallower than {ref}'s ({refMdd}).
backtesting.frase_meses: It had positive months {meses} of the time ({ref}: {refMeses}).
backtesting.causas_intro: Possible causes (hypotheses from the figures, not certainties):
backtesting.causa_persistencia: Little persistence: picking the assets that had been rising did not help; splitting equally among all of them (1/N) would have given {unoN}.
backtesting.causa_costo: Rebalancing cost: in each of its {n} rebalances it bought and sold on average {turnover} of the portfolio value; with the fee that takes away about {costo} points.
backtesting.causa_concentracion: Concentration: it put up to {max} in a single asset, so a few bets weighed a lot.
backtesting.causa_no_elegido: The reference asset that rose the most was {ticker} ({retorno}); it weighed {peso} on average in this portfolio.
backtesting.cierre: Past performance does not guarantee future results.
backtesting.cierre_profesor: This backtest uses synthetic history: the prices are not real.
backtesting.cierre_real: This backtest uses real Yahoo Finance prices; even so, the past does not repeat itself.
backtesting.recalculo_profesor: In Course mode the backtest is read from the course file and is not recomputed. Recomputing in your browser is available in Real mode.
backtesting.nota_tope_real: Note on the data: {lista} per asset, above the general cap of {tope}. In the real data it is a rule stated in the file's method, the same as in the course material.
backtesting.recalculo_real: You can recompute the backtest in your browser with the real closes, ending on another date. It uses the same monthly rule; the result may differ somewhat from the file, which was computed in Python.
backtesting.metodo_navegador: Recomputed in your browser with the real closes: rebalancing every {paso} sessions; risk estimated with the last {ventana} and a momentum filter of {momentum}; fee of {comision} bp on what is bought and sold. Conservative: minimum variance (cap {tc}); Moderate: maximum Sharpe (cap {tm}); Aggressive: maximum return (cap {ta}).

voz.ayuda_corta: Try: “go to classification”, “asset Apple” or “dark theme”.
voz.iniciado: Voice commands on. Say “help” to see what you can say.
voz.consent_texto: To understand what you say, the browser sends the audio to its speech recognition service (in Chrome and Edge, to Google or Microsoft servers). This site does not record or send audio on its own.
voz.consent_detener: You can stop them at any time with the Stop button, by saying “stop voice” or with the Esc key.
voz.no_disponible: Your browser has no speech recognition (for example, Firefox). Use Chrome or Edge for voice commands.
voz.panel_ayuda: Control the site by speaking: “go to backtesting”, “asset NVDA”, “click Trading”, “read summary”.
voz.atajo: Alt+Shift+V turns voice commands on or off.
voz.no_aqui: That command is not used on this page.
voz.no_activo: I could not find the asset “{texto}”.
voz.no_clic: I could not find “{texto}” on the page.
voz.no_entendi: I did not understand “{texto}”. Say “help” to see the commands.
voz.err_permiso: The microphone could not be used: permission was denied. The site still works with keyboard and mouse.
voz.err_red: Speech recognition needs an internet connection.
voz.err_general: Speech recognition stopped; turn it on again from the Accessibility center.

ayuda.sub: How to use the system, keyboard shortcuts, voice commands and glossary.
ayuda.inicio_1: Pick the data mode in the top bar: Professor mode (the default) uses the guide's data; Real mode uses market data.
ayuda.inicio_2: Browse the modules from the sidebar or search for them with Ctrl + K.
ayuda.inicio_3: Every prediction says UP or DOWN with its probability and uncertainty; none of them is a recommendation.
ayuda.inicio_4: Practice in Trading: it is a simulation and moves no real money.
ayuda.at_barra: Open search (when you are not typing)
ayuda.at_voz: Turn voice commands on or off
ayuda.at_esc: Close the open dialog, menu or drawer
ayuda.at_flechas: Move through tabs, lists and results
ayuda.at_tab: Go to the next or previous control
ayuda.def_volatilidad: How much an asset's returns vary, expressed per year. More volatility means more risk.
ayuda.def_beta: How sensitive the asset is to the market: above one, it moves more than the market.
ayuda.def_sharpe: Return per unit of risk: excess return divided by volatility.
ayuda.def_cvar: Average loss in the worst scenarios, beyond VaR.
ayuda.def_drawdown: The largest fall from a peak to the low that follows it.
ayuda.def_correlacion: How much two assets move together: from minus one (opposite) to one (identical).
ayuda.def_consenso: The class (UP or DOWN) chosen by most of the classification models.
ayuda.def_banda: Likely range of the prediction between the model's low and high percentiles: it shows its uncertainty.
ayuda.def_base: All curves start from the same value so returns can be compared regardless of each asset's price.
ayuda.f1_r: Not in Professor mode: it is the synthetic data from the course guide. Real mode uses downloaded market data, with its cutoff date.
ayuda.f2_r: No. Trading is a simulation with fictitious money; no order ever reaches a broker.
ayuda.f3_r: The models are binary classifiers: they predict whether the price will rise or fall over the horizon, with a probability.
ayuda.f4_r: Only in this browser. You can delete it from Profile.
ayuda.f5_p: How do I change the language or time zone?
ayuda.f5_r: With the language selector in the top bar or from Settings.
ayuda.f6_r: No. It is an educational prototype: predictions are uncertain and are not recommendations.

acerca.sub: What this system is, where its data comes from and what it was built with.
acerca.proposito: Educational prototype for the Human-Computer Interaction course (FISI-UNMSM): a simulated investing system with explained AI models, accessible and multilingual.
acerca.datos_profesor: Professor mode: synthetic data from the guide, with a cutoff of {fecha}.
acerca.datos_profesor_sin: Professor mode: synthetic data from the guide.
acerca.datos_real: Real mode: market data with a cutoff of {fecha}.
acerca.datos_real_sin: Real mode: no real data available yet.
acerca.ia: The code, the draft translations and the documentation were developed with AI assistants (Claude Code and Codex), under the supervision of Team A.
acerca.uso_mediapipe: Camera gestures (loaded only when turned on)
acerca.aviso: This is not investment advice: predictions are uncertain.
